title: How well must a nailing robot find the studs, and does measuring more beat measuring better?
summary: buildbot-fasten left stud-finding as the unmodelled term in the nailing budget. Here every nail on a stud shares that stud's position error, and a 4x8 sheet has four studs (two joints of 17 nails with a ±3.9 mm window, two intermediate studs with ±17.4 mm) and 14 plate nails, with 0.9 mm of robot scatter on each nail. Quadrature and Monte Carlo agree (within 0.01). A single read of each stud must be good to 0.89 mm (1 sigma) for 95% of sheets to land all 62 nails in their windows; at 3 mm only 31% do. A stud finder's vendor claim (‘within 1/8 in’) gives 28% clean sheets and 8 of 62 nails missed if read as 1 sigma, 69% and 1.1 missed if read as a 95% bound. Averaging n reads allows √n more scatter (3.56 mm at 16 reads); pooling the studs of a wall through a 16 in grid allows 2.95 mm for a perfectly straight wall and nothing once layout scatter reaches 4–8 mm; re-measuring at every nail is worst (0.86 mm), because 62 independent errors must all be small where a shared one is four draws. Simulated: reading and layout scatter are swept, not measured; the vendor figure is a claim with an unstated statistic; reads are assumed independent and Gaussian; no camera or wall is modelled.
lede: how well must a nailing robot find the studs? A 4x8 sheet needs a single stud reading good to 0.89 mm (1 sigma) for 95% clean sheets; a stud finder's 'within 1/8 in' claim gives 28% (8 of 62 nails missed) or 69%; averaging reads and pooling a straight wall help, re-measuring each nail is worst.
